breakfast.name: Non (Uzbek Bread)
instructions: Make dough, rise
Shape into flat rounds, stamp center with chekich
Top with seeds
Bake in tandoor
breakfast.description: Round stamped tandoor bread — sacred in Uzbek culture.

breakfast.name: Kaymak with Honey
instructions: Spread thick kaymak on warm bread
Drizzle with honey
breakfast.description: Clotted cream and honey on bread.

breakfast.name: Patir Non (Uzbek Bread)
instructions: Patir non is the enriched Uzbek flatbread -- richer than basic non
A round bread stamped with a decorative pattern in the center (using a chekich -- a bread stamp)
The edges are thick and puffy, the center is thin and decorated
Baked in a tandoor (tandir) -- the bread is slapped onto the hot clay wall
Bread (non/nan) is sacred in Uzbek culture -- it must never be placed upside down
Breaking bread together is a fundamental act of hospitality
Uzbek bread is the centerpiece of the dastarkhan (the laid table)
breakfast.description: Enriched Uzbek flatbread -- patir non, stamped with a chekich (bread stamp) pattern, baked in a tandoor. The edges puff while the center stays thin and decorated. Bread is sacred in Uzbek culture -- never placed upside down. Breaking bread is the fundamental act of hospitality.

breakfast.name: Halim (Wheat and Meat Porridge)
instructions: Halim is the Uzbek slow-cooked wheat and meat porridge
Wheat and meat cooked together for 3+ hours until the wheat dissolves
Similar to harees/haleem across the Islamic world
Topped with fried onions and a drizzle of oil
Eaten for breakfast during cold Uzbek winters
A Ramadan pre-dawn meal (suhoor) -- provides sustained energy through the fast
breakfast.description: Uzbek slow-cooked wheat and meat porridge -- halim, cracked wheat and lamb simmered for 3+ hours until the wheat dissolves. Topped with fried onions. Eaten for winter breakfast and Ramadan suhoor (pre-dawn meal) for sustained energy.

lunch.name: Plov (Pilaf)
instructions: Fry onion, brown lamb
Add julienned carrots and cumin
Add rice, water, chickpeas
Place garlic head on top
Cook covered until done
lunch.description: Uzbekistan's national dish — lamb pilaf with carrots, the centerpiece of every celebration.

lunch.name: Shurpa (Meat Broth)
instructions: Simmer lamb 45 min
Add vegetables
Cook 15 more min
Garnish with cilantro
lunch.description: Rich, clear lamb broth with large vegetables.

lunch.name: Shurpa (Lamb and Vegetable Soup)
ingredients: Lamb (bone-in pieces -- the bone gives broth depth)
instructions: Shurpa is the Uzbek lamb and vegetable soup -- a Central Asian staple
Large chunks of lamb (bone-in) simmered with whole or large-cut vegetables
The broth is clear and deeply flavored from the lamb bones
Each ingredient is cut large -- this is not a finely diced soup
Cumin and coriander are the signature Uzbek spices
Served in large bowls (kosa) -- the meat and vegetables are substantial
A cold-weather dish -- the high altitude and continental climate of Uzbekistan make warming soups essential
lunch.description: Uzbek hearty lamb soup -- shurpa, bone-in lamb simmered with large-cut vegetables in a cumin-coriander broth. Each ingredient cut large -- this is substantial, not delicate. A cold-weather essential for Uzbekistan's continental climate.

lunch.name: Manti (Steamed Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: ground lamb mixed with onion (onion proportion is high)
instructions: Manti are the Central Asian steamed dumplings -- large, substantial, and meaty
The Uzbek version: large dumplings steamed in a multi-tiered steamer (mantovarka)
The filling: lamb and onion -- the onion-to-meat ratio is nearly 1:1
The high onion content creates steam inside the dumpling, making juicy pockets
Cumin-spiced -- the unmistakable Uzbek flavor marker
Eaten with sour cream or yoghurt and sometimes a tomato sauce
Part of the Turkic dumpling family (along with Turkish manti, Korean mandu, Mongolian buuz)
lunch.description: Uzbek large steamed dumplings -- manti, lamb and onion filling (nearly 1:1 ratio -- the onion creates steam and juice inside) in thin dough, steamed in a mantovarka (tiered steamer). Cumin-spiced. Part of the Turkic dumpling family. Served with sour cream.

lunch.name: Achichuk (Fresh Tomato Salad)
ingredients: Onion (white, sliced thin and salted to remove bite)
instructions: Achichuk is the Uzbek fresh tomato and onion salad -- the standard accompaniment to plov
Ripe tomatoes cut into wedges, thinly sliced onion (salted to soften)
Sometimes hot chili peppers are added
Fresh basil and cilantro
No dressing -- the tomato juice IS the dressing
The freshness cuts through the richness of plov and grilled meats
Uzbek tomatoes (especially from the Fergana Valley) are famous for their sweetness
lunch.description: Uzbek fresh tomato salad -- achichuk, ripe tomato wedges with thin-sliced salted onion, basil, and cilantro. No dressing -- the tomato juice is the dressing. The essential accompaniment to plov. Fergana Valley tomatoes are famous for their sweetness.

dinner.name: Somsa (Baked Pastries)
ingredients: Filling: lamb, onion, cumin, black pepper, tail fat
instructions: Make layered dough
Fill with spiced lamb
Shape triangles, seal
Brush with egg, top with sesame
Bake in tandoor or at 200°C until golden
dinner.description: Flaky baked meat pastries from the tandoor.

dinner.name: Manti (Steamed Dumplings)
instructions: Roll thin wrappers
Fill generously
Pinch closed
Steam 30 min
Serve with garlic yogurt
dinner.description: Large steamed dumplings — lamb and pumpkin.

dinner.name: Lagman (Hand-Pulled Noodle Soup)
ingredients: Hand-pulled noodles (flour dough stretched and pulled by hand)
Onion, tomato, bell pepper, radish, green beans
instructions: Lagman is the Uzbek hand-pulled noodle dish -- Silk Road food at its most tangible
The noodles are hand-pulled: dough stretched, oiled, and pulled into long strands
The pulling technique requires skill and practice
The broth: a rich lamb and vegetable stew ladled over the noodles
Chinese origin (lamian) brought west along the Silk Road and adapted with Central Asian flavors
The noodles are thick and chewy -- very different from Italian pasta
Lagman exists from China (Xinjiang) through Central Asia to Turkey -- each version is different
The Uzbek version emphasizes cumin and bell pepper
dinner.description: Uzbek hand-pulled noodle soup -- lagman, dough stretched and pulled into long chewy strands, served in a rich lamb and vegetable broth. Chinese origin (lamian) adapted along the Silk Road with Central Asian cumin and peppers. Exists from Xinjiang to Turkey, each version different.

dinner.name: Tandir Kabob (Tandoor-Baked Lamb)
ingredients: Whole lamb leg or large cuts
instructions: Tandir kabob is lamb baked inside a tandoor (tandir) -- the Central Asian clay oven
Large pieces of lamb lowered into the tandir on hooks
Slow-baked for 2-3 hours in the residual heat of the clay oven
The lamb emerges fall-apart tender, smoky, and deeply flavored
The Samarkand and Bukhara versions are the most famous
Eaten at celebrations and gatherings
The tandir: an underground clay oven heated by burning wood at the bottom
dinner.description: Uzbek tandoor-baked lamb -- tandir kabob, large lamb pieces lowered on hooks into a clay oven (tandir) and slow-baked 2-3 hours. Fall-apart tender and smoky. Samarkand and Bukhara versions most famous. For celebrations. The tandir is heated by burning wood at the bottom.

dinner.name: Dimlama (Layered Meat and Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Dimlama is the Uzbek one-pot layered stew -- everything stacked in one kazan (cast iron pot)
Layers: meat at the bottom, then onion, potato, carrot, cabbage, tomato on top
No water added -- the vegetables release their moisture as they cook
The pot is sealed and slow-cooked for 2 hours
The name comes from "dim" (steam) -- the food steams in its own juices
A family meal -- the whole dinner in one pot
dinner.description: Uzbek one-pot layered stew -- dimlama (from "dim," steam), meat and vegetables stacked in a kazan (cast iron pot) with no water added. The vegetables release moisture and steam for 2 hours. A whole family dinner in one sealed pot.

snacks.name: Chuchvara (Mini Dumplings in Broth)
instructions: Make tiny dumplings
Drop into simmering broth
Cook until they float
Serve in broth with yogurt and dill

snacks.name: Samsa (Flaky Meat Pastry)
ingredients: Puff-style dough (layered with butter or lamb fat)
Filling: ground or cubed lamb, onion (lots)
instructions: Samsa is the Uzbek flaky meat pastry -- baked in the tandoor
A layered, flaky dough wrapped around a lamb and onion filling
Baked in the tandoor (stuck to the clay wall, like bread)
The tandoor heat makes the pastry layers puff and crisp
Triangular shape -- the signature samsa form
Cumin-spiced and topped with sesame seeds
Sold at every bazaar and street corner in Uzbekistan
The samsa is part of the samosa family -- from the Persian sanbosag
snacks.description: Uzbek flaky tandoor-baked meat pastry -- samsa, layered dough around cumin-spiced lamb and onion, baked on the clay tandoor wall. Triangular shape, sesame-topped. Sold at every bazaar. Part of the samosa family (from Persian sanbosag).

snacks.name: Chuchvara (Tiny Boiled Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: ground beef or lamb, onion
Sour cream or vinegar sauce (for serving)
instructions: Chuchvara are the tiny Uzbek boiled dumplings -- smaller than manti
Bite-sized dumplings filled with seasoned meat
Served in broth (as a dumpling soup) or drained with sour cream
Similar to Russian pelmeni and Chinese jiaozi
Making chuchvara is a family activity -- everyone gathers to fold
The small size means quick cooking
snacks.description: Uzbek tiny boiled dumplings -- chuchvara, bite-sized meat dumplings served in broth or with sour cream. Smaller than manti. Similar to pelmeni and jiaozi. Making them is a family gathering activity.

snacks.name: Norin (Cold Noodle and Horse Meat Dish)
ingredients: Horse meat or beef (boiled and finely shredded)
instructions: Norin is the Uzbek cold noodle dish with shredded horse meat
Thin noodles mixed with finely shredded boiled meat
Served at room temperature
Horse meat is traditional -- a Central Asian and Turkic staple
The dish is simple and austere -- nomadic origins
Served at celebrations, especially in the Tashkent region
snacks.description: Uzbek cold noodle dish -- norin, thin noodles mixed with finely shredded horse meat (or beef) and raw onion, served at room temperature. Horse meat is a Central Asian and Turkic staple. Nomadic origins. Served at celebrations in the Tashkent region.

desserts.name: Halva
instructions: Toast flour in butter until golden
Make sugar syrup
Combine, add nuts
Pour into mold, let set
desserts.description: Buttery flour halva studded with nuts.

desserts.name: Halva (Flour Halva)
instructions: Uzbek flour halva: flour toasted in butter until golden and nutty, then sweetened
A warm, crumbly, intensely buttery sweet
Different from tahini-based or semolina halva
Made for celebrations, funerals, and religious gatherings
The flour-toasting: must be stirred constantly to prevent burning
Served in slabs or pressed into molds
desserts.description: Uzbek flour halva -- flour toasted in generous butter until golden and nutty, sweetened with sugar syrup. Warm, crumbly, and intensely buttery. Different from tahini halva. Made for celebrations, funerals, and religious gatherings.

desserts.name: Chak-Chak (Fried Honey Pastry)
instructions: Chak-chak is the Central Asian and Tatar fried honey pastry
Small pieces of dough fried until golden
Bound together with hot honey into a mound or tower
The honey hardens as it cools, holding the pieces together
A celebration sweet -- weddings and holidays
Shared across Uzbek, Tatar, and Kazakh cultures
Sweet, crunchy, and sticky
desserts.description: Central Asian fried honey pastry -- chak-chak, small dough pieces fried golden and bound with hot honey into a mound. The honey hardens to hold it together. A celebration sweet for weddings and holidays. Shared across Uzbek, Tatar, and Kazakh cultures.

drinks.name: Green Tea (Ko'k Choy)
instructions: Brew green tea in lyagan
Pour back and forth three times
Serve
drinks.description: Green tea — the social fabric of Uzbek life.

drinks.name: Compot
instructions: Simmer fruits with sugar
Cool, serve cold

drinks.name: Ayran (Salted Yoghurt Drink)
instructions: Ayran is the Central Asian and Turkish salted yoghurt drink
Yoghurt thinned with water and salted
Drunk cold with meals -- especially fatty and rich dishes
The sourness and salt cut through the richness of plov and kebab
Made fresh at home or bought in cartons
A cooling drink for Uzbekistan's hot summers
drinks.description: Uzbek salted yoghurt drink -- ayran, yoghurt thinned with cold water and salted. Drunk with meals to cut through the richness of plov and kebab. A cooling drink for Uzbekistan's hot summers.
